version.value: Concert-band arrangement; arranger and edition unestablished
version.note: This is not labelled as the same orchestral scoring as the Elgar and Stock recordings. The band transfer’s shared reprise aligns two semitones below the orchestral reference; this measured pitch relationship does not identify a printed arrangement. A separate self-alignment of 81–139 against 140–199 seconds yields median confidence 0.971 without transposition (cache/analysis/elgar-pomp-circumstance-1-usmb-trio-repeat.json), supporting an additional earlier trio traversal. The three-way comparison is restricted to the later reprise and final trio.

recording.value: US-government sound recording: Commons explicitly applies PD-USGov-Military-Marines to the performance/recording
recording.note: Rule 1, recording-specific US-law basis under 17 USC §105, not worldwide CC clearance. Commons separates Performance/Recording from Composition and attributes the file to a Marine Band official-duty recording with an official .mil source. No CC-NC licence appears in the Commons record or the reviewed official source wording. Marine Band boilerplate says its institutionally distributed recordings ‘may not be distributed for private use and are not for sale’ because appropriated funds are used: this is the agency’s physical-distribution policy, not a non-commercial copyright licence on the government performance. Official web downloads are offered separately. Direct upstream retrieval returned HTTP 403 during this research; the official page’s indexed distribution wording and reader-accessible download instructions were examined, and the file’s recording-specific Commons declaration remains explicit. No claim of worldwide rights or a cleared private arrangement is made.
